key_idea: Each extra leading letter moves the direction of the remaining suffix halfway toward that letter's axis, i.e. by 90/2^(k-1) degrees, so the angle is 45-degree quadrant centre plus a signed geometric series.
sketch: Take the last two letters as the quadrant centre (45/135/225/315), then walk the remaining letters from right to left with step 22.5, 11.25, ...: subtract the step if the letter is the quadrant's lower-angle axis, add it otherwise (N counts as 360 in the NW quadrant). One-letter strings are handled directly. Answer is |a-b| folded to at most 180. O(|X|+|Y|). Although strings have 1000 letters, steps below 1e-13 are irrelevant for the 1e-6 tolerance, so plain doubles suffice and the loop can stop early; the main pitfall is the N wrap-around in the NW quadrant.
